title: Agent meta-harness becomes the cross-vendor policy plane for agents by H1 2027
body: Databricks open-sourcing Omnigent on June 13 introduces a meta-harness that sits one layer above individual coding agents and agent SDKs, wrapping Claude Code, Codex, Pi, OpenAI Agents and the Claude Agents SDK behind one interface so implementations can be swapped without rewriting. The structurally significant part is not the unified driver surface but where the guardrails live: Omnigent enforces stateful, contextual policy at the meta-harness layer itself, tracking each wrapped agent's actions and applying cost budgets, permissions and OS-level sandboxing across whichever runtime is underneath. That relocates the natural control point for enterprise agent governance upward, from per-runtime configuration scattered across each vendor's own harness to a single vendor-neutral layer that brokers, observes and constrains them all. The prediction is that this stops being one Databricks OSS project and becomes a recognized architectural tier. By H1 2027, expect at least one more independent vendor or hyperscaler to ship an agent meta-harness whose headline capability is enforcing policy (budgets, permissions, sandboxing, or audit) uniformly across two or more rival agent runtimes, or an enterprise-agent governance framework to name the meta-harness layer as the prescribed policy-enforcement point. What does NOT count: a single-vendor harness that only governs its own agents, an orchestration or routing tool with no cross-runtime guardrail enforcement, a marketing claim of multi-agent support without policy applied at the wrapping layer, or Omnigent itself merely adding more wrapped agents.
